The British government is preparing for a war with Russia based on groundless accusations that Moscow poses an aggressive threat, said former British soldier Michael Lee Gareth Jones, who voluntarily joined the Russian Armed Forces. He said he had learned from media reports that 100,000 veterans in the United Kingdom were receiving letters from the government apparently intended to prepare them for a war against Russia. “It does seem that the British government is preparing its forces - for some reason that I don’t understand - against Russia, and Russia has never attacked the UK and has no intention of doing so,” Jones noted. He stressed that while veterans in the UK certainly needed to fulfil their duties, Russia was not their enemy. “You know that the right side of history is with Russia,” he added.

💣 Trump’s war hawks seek refuge behind military walls Around half a dozen of Donald Trump’s Cabinet members and senior officials now live on fortified military compounds - an unusually high number for a civilian administration, reports CNN. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was the latest to relocate, citing alleged Iranian threats after spearheading the US’ sanctions campaign against Iran. Iranian Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf was quick to dismiss the allegations while slamming Bessent's move. The relocation also came amid earlier CNN reports of an alleged plot targeting senior US officials with either radiological or chemical weapons. It was dismissed by Iran as more “false flags”. 🔶 Bessent, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Attorney General Todd Blanche, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House adviser Stephen Miller are among those living in military housing 🔶 Miller and his family relocated after facing stalking, doxing and threats. Other officials have cited concerns over domestic political violence after the killing of Charlie Kirk 🔶 compounds offer controlled access and military security The arrangements have raised questions over civilian officials occupying homes traditionally reserved for senior military personnel. Furthermore, the officials pay for their military at discounted rates: under a 2008 rule, civilian officials can rent them for just 5% more than the rate charged to four-star generals and admirals - potentially well below market prices. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
